title: Water and the Oceans
seo_title: Earth Sciences 11: Water and the Oceans Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
short_title: the water cycle, ocean currents and groundwater
standard_text: The distribution of water has a major influence on climate and resources: the water cycle, ocean currents, groundwater and aquifers, watersheds, and properties of water. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Earth Sciences 11)
meta_desc: Free Earth Sciences 11 worksheets (BC Curriculum): the water cycle, ocean currents and groundwater. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Most of Earth's water is salt water in the oceans.
key_sub: Ocean currents move heat around the planet.
body_html:
How to think about it

About 97% of Earth's water is in the oceans; most fresh water is frozen or underground. The Sun drives the water cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, runoff and infiltration.

Surface currents are driven by wind; deep currents by differences in temperature and salinity (thermohaline circulation). Groundwater fills the pores of rock and soil; an aquifer is a layer that holds and transmits water. Porosity is how much space a rock has; permeability is how easily water flows through it.

Example

Which drives deep ocean currents?

Cold, salty water sinks.

Answer: differences in temperature and salinity

Example

Clay has high porosity but water barely moves through it. Why?

The pores are tiny and not connected.

Answer: low permeability

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up porosity and permeability.
  • Thinking most fresh water is in lakes and rivers.
  • Thinking ocean currents do not affect climate.
